{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 96,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Import Prisma before using it",
      "body": "The new credential update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws a ReferenceError whenever Salesforce client initialization reaches the update, preventing Salesforce operations."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the safeParse result",
      "body": "`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: ... }`, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Saving this result directly as `key` nests all tokens under `data`. After a successful refresh, the next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot parse the saved credentials. This also corrupts credentials when sharing is disabled; persist the result's `data` instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Define actual token fields instead of stringifying Zod schemas",
      "body": "Using `z.string().toString()` as an object key does not define a wildcard: both computed keys evaluate to the literal `[object Object]`, and the second overwrites the first. Zod also strips unknown fields by default, so a sync response containing `access_token` and `expires_in` loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom consequently calculates a NaN expiry, and Office365 cannot retain the new expiry. Define explicit supported expiry fields and preserve the required response properties."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Normalize the sync response to the callers' expected shape",
      "body": "The sync branch returns a Fetch `Response`, but several wrapped callbacks return incompatible shapes: Google and both Zoho adapters expect `.data`, while HubSpot expects a decoded token object with `accessToken` and `expiresIn`. None of those callers decodes the sync response. With syncing enabled, Google/Zoho dereference undefined and HubSpot uses undefined token fields, even when the endpoint returns valid JSON. Establish a consistent decoded response contract and adapt each caller."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 25,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a placeholder",
      "body": "This assignment runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly permits refresh responses without `refresh_token` and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. Adding the literal `refresh_token` therefore overwrites the user's valid refresh token when Microsoft omits a replacement, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when no replacement is returned."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Pass the credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint",
      "body": "`refreshOAuthTokens` interprets its third argument as a user ID and sends it as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes the credential's database ID. These IDs are unrelated. The parent application will either fail to find the user or select another user's Bigin credentials. Carry `credential.userId` through to this method and pass that instead, retaining the credential ID only for database updates."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Send the Zoom app slug rather than its integration directory name",
      "body": "The sync request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with `appId: \"zoom\"`, and the inbound webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent application using that same app identity cannot match this refresh request to the synced Zoom credentials. Pass `zoom` here."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint",
      "body": "Unlike the other adapters, Salesforce now unconditionally refreshes directly against Salesforce rather than calling `refreshOAuthTokens`. Enabling credential syncing changes its response parser but never changes the refresh destination. For credentials whose refresh token is held by the parent application, client initialization fails with an invalid refresh token even if a valid access token was synced. Use the external refresh path when configured."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Authenticate outbound credential requests",
      "body": "The request asking the parent application to return a user's OAuth access token contains only a predictable user ID and app slug. It sends neither the configured shared secret nor another authentication proof. An endpoint protected by a shared secret cannot accept these requests; an endpoint that trusts this payload alone exposes users' third-party tokens to anyone who can reach it. Add an authenticated outbound request contract rather than requiring the token-serving endpoint to trust these identifiers."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Support the minimal sync payload in Webex token validation",
      "body": "The new sync helper specifies that the endpoint should return only an access token and expiry, but this adapter still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token expiry. A response following the new contract is always rejected, so synced Webex credentials stop working when their access token expires. Add a sync-specific response path that preserves existing metadata and does not require a remotely held refresh token."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 67,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Adapt Lark refresh handling to externally managed tokens",
      "body": "Only the request destination changes here; the following code still expects Lark's nested `data` envelope and both `refresh_token` and `refresh_expires_in`. The helper's documented access-token-and-expiry response therefore fails parsing. Even if the parent supplies a Lark envelope with only those minimal fields, the saved credential loses its refresh token and the next refresh deletes it at the local refresh-token check. Handle synced credentials separately so the parent can own refresh tokens without Cal.com rejecting or deleting the integration."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Import Prisma before using it
findings.body: The new credential update references `prisma`, but this module neither imports nor declares it. This fails TypeScript checking and, if transpiled without checking, throws a ReferenceError whenever Salesforce client initialization reaches the update, preventing Salesforce operations.

findings.title: Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the safeParse result
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns `{ success: true, data: ... }`, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Saving this result directly as `key` nests all tokens under `data`. After a successful refresh, the next GoogleCalendarService instance cannot parse the saved credentials. This also corrupts credentials when sharing is disabled; persist the result's `data` instead.

findings.title: Define actual token fields instead of stringifying Zod schemas
findings.body: Using `z.string().toString()` as an object key does not define a wildcard: both computed keys evaluate to the literal `[object Object]`, and the second overwrites the first. Zod also strips unknown fields by default, so a sync response containing `access_token` and `expires_in` loses its expiry and refresh token. Zoom consequently calculates a NaN expiry, and Office365 cannot retain the new expiry. Define explicit supported expiry fields and preserve the required response properties.

findings.title: Normalize the sync response to the callers' expected shape
findings.body: The sync branch returns a Fetch `Response`, but several wrapped callbacks return incompatible shapes: Google and both Zoho adapters expect `.data`, while HubSpot expects a decoded token object with `accessToken` and `expiresIn`. None of those callers decodes the sync response. With syncing enabled, Google/Zoho dereference undefined and HubSpot uses undefined token fields, even when the endpoint returns valid JSON. Establish a consistent decoded response contract and adapt each caller.

findings.title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a placeholder
findings.body: This assignment runs even when credential sharing is disabled. Office365 explicitly permits refresh responses without `refresh_token` and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. Adding the literal `refresh_token` therefore overwrites the user's valid refresh token when Microsoft omits a replacement, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when no replacement is returned.

findings.title: Pass the credential owner's user ID to the sync endpoint
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` interprets its third argument as a user ID and sends it as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes the credential's database ID. These IDs are unrelated. The parent application will either fail to find the user or select another user's Bigin credentials. Carry `credential.userId` through to this method and pass that instead, retaining the credential ID only for database updates.

findings.title: Send the Zoom app slug rather than its integration directory name
findings.body: The sync request sends `appSlug=zoomvideo`, but Zoom credentials are created with `appId: "zoom"`, and the inbound webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent application using that same app identity cannot match this refresh request to the synced Zoom credentials. Pass `zoom` here.

findings.title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
findings.body: Unlike the other adapters, Salesforce now unconditionally refreshes directly against Salesforce rather than calling `refreshOAuthTokens`. Enabling credential syncing changes its response parser but never changes the refresh destination. For credentials whose refresh token is held by the parent application, client initialization fails with an invalid refresh token even if a valid access token was synced. Use the external refresh path when configured.

findings.title: Authenticate outbound credential requests
findings.body: The request asking the parent application to return a user's OAuth access token contains only a predictable user ID and app slug. It sends neither the configured shared secret nor another authentication proof. An endpoint protected by a shared secret cannot accept these requests; an endpoint that trusts this payload alone exposes users' third-party tokens to anyone who can reach it. Add an authenticated outbound request contract rather than requiring the token-serving endpoint to trust these identifiers.

findings.title: Support the minimal sync payload in Webex token validation
findings.body: The new sync helper specifies that the endpoint should return only an access token and expiry, but this adapter still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token expiry. A response following the new contract is always rejected, so synced Webex credentials stop working when their access token expires. Add a sync-specific response path that preserves existing metadata and does not require a remotely held refresh token.

findings.title: Adapt Lark refresh handling to externally managed tokens
findings.body: Only the request destination changes here; the following code still expects Lark's nested `data` envelope and both `refresh_token` and `refresh_expires_in`. The helper's documented access-token-and-expiry response therefore fails parsing. Even if the parent supplies a Lark envelope with only those minimal fields, the saved credential loses its refresh token and the next refresh deletes it at the local refresh-token check. Handle synced credentials separately so the parent can own refresh tokens without Cal.com rejecting or deleting the integration.
